minutes.headline: Commission approved a hallway/siding renovation at 936 Mass Ave and vetted a prospective new member
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission met by Zoom with a prospective new resident, Patricia Porter, describing renovations at 936 Massachusetts Avenue, and voted to approve a determination of applicability for that work. The commission also interviewed a prospective volunteer commissioner, Andrew Gillis, about joining, and discussed plans to meet in person with the owners of a deteriorating former church at 50 Main Street and to shift its next meeting to the third Thursday of April.

public_comment.stated_role: future resident / property owner at 936 Massachusetts Avenue
public_comment.topic: Described plans to add a hallway connecting the main house and barn, replace deteriorated wood siding with Hardie board, demolish a non-structural chimney, and eventually build a garage, while preserving the original narrow staircase as a feature.

votes.motion: Motion to approve the determination of applicability for 936 Massachusetts Avenue
Motion to approve the meeting minutes from the 12th February 2026 meeting

budget_items.topic: Town override vote (context for volunteer scheduling)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair noted the select board and town manager were consumed with budget discussions with the finance and school committees because the town is likely to have an override vote, which could affect how quickly a new commission volunteer gets appointed.

decisions.decision: Commission will meet in person with the owners of 50 Main Street at the April 16th meeting regarding the deteriorating former church steeple/base.
Next meeting moved from the second Thursday to the third Thursday of April due to the chair's travel.
Nathan will send a second letter to the 50 Main Street property owners by the end of next week.
Commission anticipates Andrew Gillis could be appointed to the commission by the April meeting if he reviews the bylaw/guidelines and submits the volunteer form.

what_happened.line: Commission approved a determination of applicability for renovation work at 936 Massachusetts Avenue, voting 3-0.
Commission plans to meet in person in April with the owners of the deteriorating former church at 50 Main Street over demolition-by-neglect concerns.
Commission interviewed a prospective new commissioner, Andrew Gillis, and anticipates he could be appointed by the April meeting.
Next meeting is shifting from the second to the third Thursday of April because of the chair's travel.

why_it_matters: Property owners doing exterior work in the historic district need a determination of applicability like the one approved for 936 Massachusetts Avenue.
The former church at 50 Main Street is a landmark building the commission is trying to protect from further deterioration, and owner cooperation is still pending a second letter.
Filling the commission's open seat affects how quickly future applications get reviewed, and the chair noted town budget-season demands could slow that appointment.
